review: Second intensive review of registry-labelled Python loaders and DingTalk Workspace CLI
method: Static code/AST, filefacts (including decoded text), UPX unpacking, Rizin disassembly, PE import and Authenticode analysis. No specimen code was executed.

execution_trace: At module load: sleep ten seconds, construct a Solana JSON-RPC getSignaturesForAddress request and retrieve up to 1000 signatures for the configured address.
Select the first truthy memo, parse it as JSON and Base64-decode its link value into the second request URL. This supplies a mutable blockchain rendezvous rather than a fixed payload host.

The second request supplies platform.system() as an os header. Its response secretkey header and Base64-decoded ivbase64 header become globals. The Base64-decoded response body is passed directly to exec in that namespace.
The local file is already decoded Python. It contains no AES decryption operation; the key/IV variables may be consumed by the acquired code. No claim is made about the final payload.
samples.judgement: The module has no application function besides blockchain-selected, unsigned remote code execution. This covert discovery/activation chain tips the judgement despite missing final-stage bytes and deployment context.
samples.coverage: Two existing hostile findings cover the blockchain rendezvous and decoded remote activation, plus suspicious Base64-to-exec. Retained without editing.
samples.limitation: filefacts reports flow-field-unavailable/flow-query-incomplete for with-bindings; manual source tracing establishes the response-to-exec relationship. Default ML says benign (L5000), a classifier miss despite accurate hostile traits.

samples.identification: DingTalk Workspace CLI v1.0.63-0.20260916084311-ed770d648d04 with Alibaba SecurityGuardSDK 1.0.70.3341
execution_trace: Go runtimepayload verifies a fixed embedded container, extracts only the allowed native library and its manifest into a private cache, checks digests and atomically publishes the cache. Windows startNative calls LoadLibrary, GetProcAddress(k9Xm2pQv), registers a callback and passes environment zero plus that callback.

runtimecontext.Resolve initializes once, accepts a bounded UTF-8 token through the callback and returns redacted status on failure or timeout. HeaderValue serializes the token as {umid:...}; the HTTP client sends it in x-dingtalk-ext, and login URLs may carry callerUmt/caller=dws.

Both Windows libraries carry intact, cryptographically verified Alibaba (China) Network Technology Authenticode signatures. ARM64 exposes SecurityGuardSDK version data and its build PDB path. The AMD64 file unpacks normally with UPX; its exports and implementation agree with the SDK interface. All five platform-library SHA-256 values match the shipped manifest.

AMD64 export k9Xm2pQv at VA 0x1800fd0a0 registers the supplied callback in a vector and dispatches initialization. Obfuscated jump tables and 1265 adjacent inverse-branch pairs in .text deliberately skip dead bytes; these are protector behavior, retained as suspicious.

CoCreateInstance at VA 0x1801a50e0 receives CLSID 4590f811-1d3a-11d0-891f-00aa004b2e24 (WMI locator), followed by WMI automation. SHGetFolderPathA at 0x1803c2910 requests CSIDL 0x23 (ProgramData), with fallback C:\ProgramData and Alibaba\AlibabaProtectDT subdirectory. These are not evidence of user-profile COM payload activation or a scheduled task.

WinHTTP path at 0x180003df8 opens a connection/request and reads response bytes into a growing heap buffer at 0x180005224. The conditional setup at 0x180003e7e writes mask 0x3100 into one frame local, passes that same local and option 31/length 4 to WinHttpSetOption. Added a notable detection binding the local, mask, option and IAT target.

The SDK includes WMI hardware/OS/display queries, registry reads, per-target Windows Credential Manager operations, crypto and vendor HTTP endpoints. Existing dual-use capability detections remain. The examined paths fit anti-fraud device-token generation, not an established credential-exfiltration or payload-execution chain.
samples.judgement: A purpose-consistent wrapper, intact vendor-signed SDKs, matching distribution hashes and traced WMI/cache behavior outweigh packing, opaque export names and generic API co-occurrence. No deployment context or independent audit of every protected SDK path is available; benign is a balance-of-evidence judgement, not a signature-based allowlist.
samples.dependency_review: The fetched githubassets code-view JavaScript is a minified GitHub web UI asset reached through the repository LICENSE page, not a distributed SDK payload. It had no hostile or suspicious finding in either followed scan.
samples.coverage: Removed two unsupported hostile claims. Preserved API observations in a neutral notable composite and moved embed/digest facts to their actual metadata subjects. Added suspicious disassembly obstruction and notable conditional certificate-ignore coverage. No vendor allowlist was added.

execution_trace: Module-level time.sleep(86400) delays execution by one day.

subprocess.run launches argv [sh,-c,curl x|sh]. The explicit -c makes the third argument a shell program: curl output is fed directly to a second shell. The subprocess is real shell execution even though Python passes an argv list.
samples.judgement: Only behavior is delayed, unauthenticated network-to-interpreter activation, with no ordinary CLI/library purpose. The bare x host is unresolved here and may be a placeholder; runtime success, final payload and deployment context remain unknown. Static attack-pattern evidence supports malicious.
samples.coverage: Two existing hostile composites and two suspicious timing findings remain accurate and unchanged. The hostile composites overlap on one delayed-loader pattern; the file does not justify inventing additional independent hostile actions to inflate coverage.

rule_changes.change: Same matcher, type scope, size cap and exclusions; hostile to notable, removed unsupported T1105/T1053.005/B0024 claims. Imports/co-occurrence do not bind staging, destination or activation. Actual benign counterexample is signed SecurityGuardSDK; inert import-only control corroborates it.

Preserved matcher, scope and notable severity. Describes directive text, not platform selection, hiding or execution. Chose source-directive metadata rather than build-role metadata to avoid granting broad metadata/build suppressors to embedded assets.
Preserved matcher, scope and notable severity; description explicitly records a SHA-256-shaped value rather than verification.
Retired composite. Embedding + a digest map + stock UPX establishes no trust violation or inspection evasion. Its three observations remain detected; no supported attack technique was removed.
At least eight inverse short-jump pairs with the same forward destination, bounded to executable PE sections. Suspicious; no vendor/family/filename dependency.
Notable PE64 IAT-bound call setup. Requires matching initialization/addressed frame local, certificate-ignore bits, option 31, size four, and WinHttpSetOption import target.

consumer_audit: Searched exact IDs and every source ancestor. No exact consumers of the retired Go composite or its atoms. Source-parent selectors in JS/package/Python rules have incompatible effective file scope for these source/JSON/PE facts; no concealed-payload semantics were copied to the new metadata atoms.

Preserved the WinHTTP profile in the hosts-security-sinkhole positive alternative and in CrystalX’s existing named exception group, retaining former parent-directory membership without extra suppressor inflation.

New WinHTTP composite implies the existing winhttp-request-response-flow descendant, so destination HTTP-client directory selectors gain no new population or cardinality role. The directive destination has one broad PHP-only source-syntax consumer, incompatible with its retained Go/source scope. No package/integrity ancestor consumer was found.

New suspicious branch evidence was rescanned across archive members; no new hostile composite fired. External malicious sample a588c91e390e2f7bd7eac6c793f752cf067f87c4a9f0cded2b61c00a4e1bbb42 retains its four hostile/suspicious findings and ML probability 0.98. Its original file disappeared during review; forager recovered identical bytes from Hopper, with provenance retained in scratch. The existing Elex positive-all-profiles PE also retains all findings and its score.
comparison_limits: Initial scans followed the configured external-reference fetch graph. A followed post-edit scan was also retained as *.after.with-follow.json; the fetched GitHub asset set grew by six nodes during revalidation. Final scans use --follow=none to isolate the immutable input and archive members. Scores for followed and local-only archive reports differ slightly.

No supported hostile/suspicious finding was lost in either Python sample or the external positive controls. The only hostile losses in the archive are the two refuted claims; the neutral replacement and relocated metadata observations remain.

Unchanged fseek-text/file-position-api findings disappear from compact atomscan output on AMD64/upx nodes. cleave test-rules still reports both matched and explicitly identifies low-value any/needs filtering for file-position-api. This is an unresolved reporting discrepancy, not removal or weakening of those matchers; it establishes no attack-coverage loss.

The default ML verdict remains benign for selector-decoded.py despite probability 0.9952286 and two accurate hostile traits; it first flags at L5000. bomb.py is ML-hostile at L1. The archive remains ML-benign. Models identify as v18.18 while the extractor warns it produces v19 features; the classifier gap was not masked with duplicate or inaccurate rules.

validation.note: Run as final action after judgement markers. No runtime success is claimed.
